facts.fact: News Moris, carrying Defi Media's account of the Prime Minister's reply in the National Assembly, reports that the Crime Occurrence Tracking System was introduced in 2011 to manage and track complaints.
The report has the Prime Minister saying all police stations are equipped with personal computers used for the Crime Occurrence Tracking System; no count of stations is given.

The report has the Prime Minister announcing that the Crime Occurrence Tracking System, improved but never replaced since 2011, is to be replaced by a new case management system, with a specialised consultant to be hired on the Central Informatics Bureau's recommendation; no date or budget for that replacement is given.

systems.tiers: Personal computers in all police stations

systems.platform: Not named; operational since 1999, never modernised
systems.tiers: Terminals in all police stations; Rs 43 million in the 2025-2026 budget for a new integrated system with biometric data, tender by end of August 2025, live within two years

systems.platform: Operated by Mauritius Telecom under a lease
systems.tiers: Footage reviewed from station computers; upgrade scheduled December 2025

systems.platform: Maintained and upgraded by Brinks Ltd under a rental agreement

note: A syndicated press account of the same parliamentary reply as document 13 (Hansard, 17 June 2025); the Rs 43 million is for the criminal records database, not for the station records system.
